note: Three modes, each heard against its parent and then found by its one changed note: Mixolydian against major, Dorian against natural minor, Phrygian over a drone, each section with its own feel to reach and the last ending on a line the learner makes up. The text names the changed note as a dot the staff rings, never the letter the tool already shows. Missing: a listening tool that plays two scales one after the other for any instrument (the guitar-play-along's two-scales stands in, listened to only).

exercise.title: Modes by the one note that changes
exercise.why: Each mode is plain major or minor with one note changed, so once you hear that one note against the root, you hear the mode.

cells.text: Press Play below to start the backing track: {{chord:I}} for eight bars, four in G major, then four in G Mixolydian. Follow the notes view and listen for the bar where one note changes.

The note that changed is {{b7}}, a half step under the {{7}} of major. Tap {{1}}, then the ringed {{b7}}, then {{1}} again on the staff below.
Practice until you can hum {{b7}} before you tap it.

Press Play below to start the backing track: {{chord:i}} for eight bars, four in D natural minor, then four in D Dorian. This time the note that changes is {{6}}, a half step over the {{b6}} of natural minor.

Tap {{1}}, then the ringed {{6}} on the staff below. Then tap up the scale from {{1}} and stop on {{6}}.
Practice until the stop on {{6}} sounds bright to you, not dark.

Phrygian is natural minor with a lowered 2nd, {{b2}}, a half step above the root.
Press Play below to start the drone on E. Tap {{1}}, the ringed {{b2}} and {{1}} again on the staff under it. Then tap a line of your own that keeps coming back to {{b2}}.
Practice until you hear the half step from {{b2}} down to {{1}} as soon as it comes.
